name: North Fork Nine Mile Campground (DNR)
note: Secluded WA DNR campground by a forest stream in the Loomis State Forest, about 10 miles from Loomis via the steep Toats Coulee Road. About 9-11 sites, roughly half pull-through and most good for rigs under 30 ft, vault toilet; no water or hookups. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. CLOSED as of 2026-09-29: the whole Loomis State Forest was closed for the Sinlahekin Fire. --Claude

name: Indian Camp (DNR, Teanaway)
note: WA DNR campground in the Teanaway Community Forest north of Cle Elum, in an open pine clearing near the Middle Fork Teanaway River, close to Forest Service trailheads. 11 sites plus group sites (some for horse groups), vault toilet; no hookups. A 25-ft travel trailer is the longest reported. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. CLOSED as of 2026-09-29: DNR says it remains closed because of flood damage at the access bridge. --Claude

name: 29 Pines Campground (DNR, Teanaway)
note: Large, open WA DNR campground in the Teanaway Community Forest on North Fork Teanaway Road north of Cle Elum, near the North Fork Teanaway River. 59 roomy sites among ponderosa pine, drinking water, restroom and vault toilets; no hookups or garbage service. Rigs of 30+ ft are reported. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. In 2026 only the south half was open and campfires were banned. --Claude

name: Middle Waddell Campground (DNR, Capitol Forest)
note: WA DNR campground in Capitol State Forest southwest of Olympia, the main hub for its ~90 miles of motorized trails - expect ORVs. About 24-33 gravel sites in three loops, mostly narrow pull-throughs good for trailers to about 27 ft, vault toilets, camp host; no water or hookups. Season May 1 to late November; 7-day limit. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. CLOSED for summer 2026 for hazard-tree removal (checked 2026-09-29). --Claude

name: Rock Creek Campground (DNR, Loup Loup)
note: Small WA DNR campground in Loup Loup Canyon west of Okanogan, 3.9 miles up the two-lane dirt Loup Loup Canyon Road from SR-20, near Loup Loup Creek. Eight gravel sites on a loop, drinking water, vault toilet, day-use shelter; no hookups. Popular in hunting season; ATVs on forest roads only. No published length limit - the loop and spurs look long enough for a mid-size trailer. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. --Claude

name: Sweat Creek Campground (DNR, Sportsmans Camp)
note: Small WA DNR campground (also called Sportsman's Camp) in the Loup Loup State Forest, a mile up Sweat Creek Road from SR-20 between Okanogan and Loup Loup Pass. Five sites in an open gravel clearing by a small stream, shelter, vault toilets; no water or hookups. Popular in hunting season; ATVs on forest roads only. One directory lists it as permanently closed while DNR still shows it open - check before relying on it. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. --Claude

name: Rocky Lake Campground (DNR)
note: Tiny WA DNR campground on quiet, non-motorized Rocky Lake east of Colville, down 2.5 miles of one-lane gravel off Artman-Gibson Road. Five sites among rock formations at the water, drinking water, vault toilet; no hookups. Catch-and-release fishing after June 1. SMALL-RIG CAUTION: one site has taken a 25-ft trailer; the others are hemmed in by rocks. First come, first served; a Discover Pass is required. --Claude

name: Manistee River RV Resort & Marina
note: RV park and marina at 20 Park Avenue in Manistee, on the Manistee River where it meets Manistee Lake, with boat access to Lake Michigan: waterfront, pull-through, full-hookup, water/electric and primitive sites, rental units, 50 marina slips, a boat ramp and a fish-cleaning station. The operator's posted hours show it closed for remodeling Nov 1, 2026 - Jan 1, 2027, reopening Jan 2 (read 2026-10-22). --Claude

name: James Creek RV Resort
note:
RJourney-run campground (formerly Pioneer Family Campground) minutes west of Raystown Lake (Huntingdon Co): 20/30/50-amp pull-through and back-in sites, many seasonal in the wooded ring, plus pool, mini golf, restaurant and cabins; near Seven Points and the Allegrippis bike trails. Open April to October 15; office closed Mon-Tue. Good Sam 8.7; Google 4.3 over 119 reviews. --Claude
MINIMUM STAY: the operator's FAQ says 'Cabins and Transit sites have a 2-day minimum' (read 2026-10-20). --Claude

name: Beaver Crossing Park Campground
note: Village of Beaver Crossing campground in the town park, entered at 1025 Elk St by the baseball field and playground. Electric and water (water in the warm months) at the RV sites; first come, first served, pay in the box at the entrance or at the village clerk's office. No dump station. --Claude

name: Du Quoin State Fairgrounds Campground
note: Illinois Department of Agriculture campground inside Gate 3 at the north end of the Du Quoin State Fairgrounds (off US 51), along the fairgrounds lake: over 1,000 sites with water and 30/50-amp electric, two bathhouses with showers, two dump stations, pavilions, fishing docks. Open April-Oct 31, first come first served (no reservations) outside the late-summer fair. --Claude

name: Swan Falls River Access (Idaho Power)
note: Idaho Power river-access area just below Swan Falls Dam on the Snake River (Snake River Birds of Prey NCA): 15 designated RV/tent sites, first-come first-served, 14-day limit; vault toilet, fire rings, boat ramp and boarding platform; no water or electric. --Claude

name: Beaver Canyon Campground
note: In-town RV park and campground at 1419 200 N in Beaver, about 55 sites. RV Life 4.5*/$$ (as Beaver Canyon RV Park). Camper-reported rate: $40 a night (Campendium, April 2024). --Claude

name: Maple Hollow Campground
note: Fishlake National Forest campground above Holden: about 10 first-come first-served RV/tent sites in maple and fir at ~7,000 ft, drinking water, vault toilets, open late May to early September, 14-day limit. Reached by 5 miles of narrow, winding gravel Maple Hollow Road from I-15 (second Holden exit) - about 30 minutes; muddy after rain. Campendium's longest reported rig is 34 ft. --Claude

name: Lakes RV
note:
RV park on US-41 (S Tamiami Trl) beside Lakes Regional Park, Fort Myers, on a lake; the operator calls itself an extended-stay community (travel nurses, trades, snowbirds) and also sells monthly and annual sites. --Claude
PEAK-SEASON MINIMUM: January-March arrivals booked online need 90 nights; single nights sell April-December (read 2026-10-21). --Claude

name: Colossal Cave Mountain Park
note: Pima County-owned park (concession-run) on Old Spanish Trail east of Vail. RV/car camping first-come first-served, at about 30 individual sites in Posta Quemada canyon (CCC-built picnic areas El Bosquecito and La Selvilla, with tables and grills; water and restrooms there). No hookups. Check in and pay at the Cave Shop first; park hours 8am-4pm and the front gates are locked at night. Pin is the cave parking lot; the camping areas are in the canyon below it and could not be located precisely. --Claude

name: Fisher's Landing Resort
note: Marina resort on Martinez Lake (Colorado River backwater) north of Yuma. Dry camping 2 weeks $75 or $150/month for 2 people; first-come first-served, pay at the Camp Rental Office. No hookups or marked pads: campers spread out across open desert above the marina, most parked by a shade tree, with roomy, private spacing. Dump station, drinking water, restrooms, showers and laundry nearby; general store sells firewood. --Claude

Fees: +$10/night each adult over 2, children 12 and under free

name: Carters Landing (Idaho Power)
note: Idaho Power camping area on the Oregon shore of Oxbow Reservoir, 3 mi downstream of McCormick Park: semi-developed, no defined sites, no hookups, vault toilet, gravel boat launch. First-come first-served at the fee station (cash/check). --Claude

name: Annett's Mono Village
note: Resort at the west end of Upper Twin Lake, 13425 Twin Lakes Rd, Bridgeport: 250+ first-come sites (no reservations), hookup sites for 2 and dry sites; marina and store. Seasonal (summer). --Claude

name: Cassel Campground (PG&E)
note: FCFS and reservable no-hookup sites in pines near Hat Creek (fly fishing) at Cassel, east of Burney; vault toilets, potable water. PG&E reservation system 2026-27: pads 35-60 ft. --Claude  Reservations need at least 2 nights; first-come, first-served sites can be taken for one night (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude

name: Cool Springs Campground (PG&E)
note: On the east shore of Butt Valley Reservoir (PG&E), Plumas County; no hookups, vault toilets; 5 mph boating. PG&E reservation system 2026-27: pads 20-35 ft. --Claude  Road work on Butt-Prattville Road near Cool Springs, Ray Adams Boat Launch and Ponderosa Flat from Aug 10, 2026 through the rest of the 2026 season: traffic delays, heavy trucks, noise and dust (PG&E notice, 2026-10-10). --Claude  Reservations need at least 2 nights; first-come, first-served sites can be taken for one night (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude

name: Lower Blue Lake Campground (PG&E)
note: High-country PG&E campground on Lower Blue Lake, ~11 mi up gravel Blue Lakes Rd off SR-88 (Carson Pass); vault toilets, piped water, bear boxes; earthen boat ramp. PG&E reservation system 2026-27: pads 25-55 ft. --Claude  Reservations need at least 2 nights; first-come, first-served sites can be taken for one night (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude

name: Middle Creek Campground (PG&E, Blue Lakes)
note: Two PG&E loops on Middle Creek between Upper and Lower Blue Lakes (Middle Creek, 5 sites, and Middle Creek Expansion, 34 sites for RVs up to 45 ft), ~11 mi up gravel Blue Lakes Rd off SR-88; vault toilets, piped water, bear boxes. PG&E reservation system 2026-27: pads 20-55 ft. --Claude  Reservations need at least 2 nights; first-come, first-served sites can be taken for one night (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude

name: Northshore Campground (PG&E, Lake Britton)
note: On a wooded point on the north shore of Lake Britton, across from McArthur-Burney Falls SP; 29 sites, no hookups. PG&E reservation system 2026-27: pads 30-80 ft. --Claude  Reservations need at least 2 nights; first-come, first-served sites can be taken for one night (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude

name: Philbrook Campground (PG&E)
note: On Philbrook Reservoir in Lassen NF above Paradise/Magalia (reached by dirt road off Humbug Rd); 20 sites, car-top boat launch, vault toilets, non-potable water only, no bear boxes. PG&E reservation system 2026-27: pads 20-55 ft. --Claude  Reservations need at least 2 nights; first-come, first-served sites can be taken for one night (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude

name: Pogie Point Campground (PG&E, Lake Pillsbury)
note: FCFS PG&E campground on the northwest corner of Lake Pillsbury (Mendocino NF); 45 shaded sites best suited to tents; vault toilets, water, boat launch nearby. PG&E reservation system 2026-27: pads 20-25 ft. --Claude  All sites first-come, first-served; no reservations (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude

name: Ruling Creek Campground (PG&E)
note: FCFS PG&E campground on the Pit River (fly fishing) below Pit 5 Dam, Shasta County; 8 drive-in sites to 45 ft. PG&E reservation system 2026-27: pads 45 ft. --Claude  All sites first-come, first-served; no reservations (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude

name: Sunset Point Campground (PG&E, Lake Pillsbury)
note: FCFS PG&E campground on the west shore of Lake Pillsbury near the Pillsbury Pines boat launch; 54 sites (14 doubles), vault toilets. PG&E reservation system 2026-27: pads 20-55 ft. --Claude  All sites first-come, first-served; no reservations (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude

name: Trout Creek Campground (PG&E)
note: Reservable PG&E campground near the Eel River below Lake Pillsbury; small RVs only (pads 16-25 ft, trailers not allowed in the lower loop); no hookups, vault toilets. PG&E reservation system 2026-27: pads 16-25 ft. --Claude  Closed early on Aug 10, 2026 for wildfire risk and water-system issues (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude  Reservations need at least 2 nights; first-come, first-served sites can be taken for one night (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude

name: Upper Blue Lake Campground (PG&E)
note: PG&E campground at the north end of Upper Blue Lake, ~12 mi up gravel Blue Lakes Rd off SR-88; vault toilets, piped water, bear boxes; earthen boat ramp. PG&E reservation system 2026-27: pads 25-50 ft. --Claude  Reservations need at least 2 nights; first-come, first-served sites can be taken for one night (PG&E, 2026-10-10). --Claude

name: Eagles Landing Campground
note: Year-round campground on Avalanche Rd just north of Sturgis (2881 Avalanche Rd): back-in gravel RV sites, tent sites, cabins with baths; a Sturgis Rally base that is open all year. Online booking (ResNexus). --Claude  MINIMUM STAY: 2 nights in the booking engine (read by AWH 2026-10-03; the home page says one night is fine). --Claude

name: Bear Lake Campground (Manawa)
note: Campground with a bar and restaurant on Bear Lake, on WI-22 north of Manawa: about 100 RV sites - basic 30-amp water/electric (50-amp on sites 91-97), lakeview, lakefront (many beside the grassy beach) and 50-amp full-hookup sites (401-412 along the highway behind a tree line) - plus deluxe cabins and seasonal sites. --Claude  MINIMUM STAY: 2 nights on every stay (Campspot, checked 2026-10-11 on an October Tuesday). --Claude

name: Beech Lake Campground
note: Go Camp Tennessee campground (Google still calls it Beech Lake Family Camping Resort) on a wooded peninsula in Beech Lake near Lexington: about 50 RV sites - 30-amp water/electric (to 42 ft), 30/50-amp pull-throughs, two lakeside sites and two water-only sites - plus a lake-view cabin; boat slips at the point. --Claude  MINIMUM STAY: 2 nights on every stay (Campspot, checked 2026-10-11 on an October Tuesday). --Claude

name: Domaine du Lac Libby
note: About 350-site wooded campground on Lac Libby at Saint-Étienne-de-Bolton (A-10 exit 100), roughly 90 traveller sites (0-, 2- and 3-service) and a seasonal section; beach on the lake; cannabis-free. Mont des Huards has 30/50A; booked online. --Claude  MINIMUM STAY: 2 nights on every stay (reservationcamping.ca, June and July 2027 weeknights, checked 2026-10-12). --Claude

name: Wabasso Campground
note: Parks Canada campground in Jasper NP on Highway 93A 16 km south of Jasper, about 230 sites (50 electric). Closed to the public for 2026 after the 2024 wildfire while Parks Canada plans its rebuild; contractors only, no public reopening date (read 2026-10-19). --Claude
